title: GET /api/crm serves every lead's full phone, secondary phone and email to the associate role, which does not hold customers.view_full_phone
actor: STAFF role=associate (assoc@pawspace.test, app_users row, permissions from lib/platform-security.ts defaultRoles)
request:
Two calls, same session.
(1) gateway: authorizeApiRequest(new Request("https://uat.pawspace.in/api/crm", {headers:{"oai-authenticated-user-email":"assoc@pawspace.test","oai-authenticated-user-full-name":"Probe%20Staff","oai-authenticated-user-full-name-encoding":"percent-encoded-utf-8"}}), {DB:db})
(2) handler: GET https://uat.pawspace.in/api/crm with the same headers, via app/api/crm/route.ts GET
d1_before: crm_contacts: 1 row CU-VICTIM / 'Meera Shah' / primary_phone '+919845012345' / secondary_phone '+919845099999' / email 'meera.shah@example.com'. app_users: USR-ASSOC assoc@pawspace.test role_code='associate' status='active'.
d1_after: Unchanged (read-only route). The exposure is in the response body, not the database.
repeatable: yes - run twice, identical 200 with the same unmasked primary_phone, secondary_phone and email both times
canonical_failure: app/api/crm/route.ts, GET: `const result=await db.prepare("SELECT * FROM crm_contacts ORDER BY updated_at DESC LIMIT 100").all<Record<string,unknown>>();` followed by `return Response.json({contacts});` - the row is returned verbatim after `await authorize(request,"customers.view")` and no `hasPermission(actor.permissions,"customers.view_full_phone")` reveal test is ever applied. The sibling customer console does exactly that test at app/api/subscription-customers/route.ts:42 `const reveal=hasPermission(actor.permissions,"customers.view_full_phone");` and masks with maskPhone/maskName when it is false. lib/platform-security.ts defines the associate role as 'Handles assigned customers and bookings with masked contact data' and grants it customers.view but NOT customers.view_full_phone.
money_consequence: No direct money movement. The exposed asset is the marketable contact list: every lead's mobile, alternate mobile and email in one 100-row page, exportable by any associate-level account (the platform's lowest customer-facing staff tier). Cost is regulatory/reputational - an unmasked-PII disclosure to a role the platform itself defines as masked - plus the commercial value of the lead list if an associate walks with it.
blast_radius: Every crm_contacts row, capped at 100 per call and unbounded across calls; every actor holding customers.view without customers.view_full_phone (associate today, plus manager which also lacks view_full_phone). Both the staff CRM screen and any script driving /api/crm.
status: FIXED (phone/name); email exposure OPEN pending a product decision
regression: tests/ptja-w2b-exposure-regressions.test.mjs :: "W2B-C01: the CRM contact list masks phones for an actor without customers.view_full_phone" + "W2B-C01: an actor with customers.view_full_phone still sees the CRM numbers"
fix_note: Masked at the route, applying the convention app/api/subscription-customers/route.ts already carries: reveal = hasPermission(actor.permissions,'customers.view_full_phone'), then maskPhone/maskName. PARTIAL BY DESIGN: email is NOT masked - the platform defines only maskPhone and maskName - and whether an associate should see a customer's email at all is a product decision left open, the same call as for Customer 360. Both primary and secondary phone are masked.

title: A preferred-channel-only preference write erases the customer's recorded service-update opt-out, and the next suppressed message is queued for delivery
actor: STAFF role=admin (ops.admin@pawspace.test) via POST /api/communications action=preference (gateway maps this action to customers.manage)
d1_before:
communication_preferences: [{"customer_id":"CUST-OPTOUT","service_updates":0,"marketing":0,"preferred_channel":null,"timezone":"Asia/Kolkata","source":"customer_self_service_opt_out","updated_at":1787689209641}]
communication_outbox: [] (the suppressed message k-before got no outbox row)
d1_after:
communication_preferences: [{"customer_id":"CUST-OPTOUT","service_updates":null,"marketing":null,"preferred_channel":"email","timezone":"Asia/Kolkata","source":"staff_governed_change","updated_at":1787689209650}]  <-- BOTH opt-outs are now NULL
communication_messages: [{"id":"MSG-BB6096CF-2FBB-","purpose":"service_recovery","status":"suppressed","idempotency_key":"k-before"},{"id":"MSG-8C3DB399-B3CC-","purpose":"service_recovery","status":"queued","idempotency_key":"k-after"}]
communication_outbox: [{"message_id":"MSG-8C3DB399-B3CC-","status":"queued"}]
repeatable: yes - the probe runs the whole sequence twice in two fresh worlds (RUN1, RUN2); byte-identical outcomes, suppressed then queued both times
canonical_failure: lib/communication-engine.ts setCommunicationPreference: `ON CONFLICT(customer_id) DO UPDATE SET service_updates=excluded.service_updates,marketing=excluded.marketing,preferred_channel=excluded.preferred_channel,source=excluded.source,updated_at=excluded.updated_at` - every column is overwritten from the incoming row unconditionally, with no COALESCE(excluded.x, service_updates). The caller feeds it NULL for anything the request omitted: app/api/communications/route.ts POST action=="preference" builds `serviceUpdates:typeof body.serviceUpdates==="boolean"?body.serviceUpdates:null` and `marketing:typeof body.marketing==="boolean"?body.marketing:null`. The absent field is therefore written as 'no recorded decision' rather than left alone. The erased value is then read back by `consent()` in the same file, and the suppression test `if(["transactional","service_recovery"].includes(input.purpose)&&c.serviceUpdates===false)` no longer fires because null !== false - unknown is treated as permission to send.
money_consequence: Messaging spend on contacts who asked not to be contacted (each queued WhatsApp/SMS is billed per message), plus the compliance exposure of transactional/service-recovery messaging to a customer whose opt-out the platform holds an audit trail for. The marketing opt-out is erased in the same write; marketing happens to stay suppressed because unknown consent also blocks marketing, so the money leak is on the transactional/service_recovery side, which fails open.
blast_radius: Any customer whose communication_preferences row is touched by a staff preference write that does not restate every consent flag - including a channel-only change, a marketing-only change, or a service-updates-only change. One call per customer; a bulk preference tool would erase consent for a whole segment. It also silently destroys the consent record itself, so the prior decision cannot be recovered from this table afterwards.
regression: tests/ptja-w2b-consent-regressions.test.mjs :: "W2B-C02: a channel-only preference write preserves the recorded opt-out" + "W2B-C02: an explicit consent change still applies, in both directions"
fix_note: The preference upsert now COALESCEs each consent column against its recorded value, so a field the caller never mentioned keeps what it had. The route deliberately distinguishes 'set to false' from 'not mentioned' by passing null, and the upsert was throwing that distinction away. An explicit change still applies in both directions.

title: CRM automation frequency cap of 0 disables the cap entirely - the strictest setting the API accepts produces unlimited marketing dispatches
actor: STAFF role=admin (ops.admin@pawspace.test) - save_policy needs customers.manage, which admin and manager hold
response:
save_policy -> 200 {"ok":true,"policyKey":"marketing:whatsapp"} (0 is accepted; validation only rejects negatives)
queue x5 with cap 0 -> [{"i":1,"status":201,"queued":true,"reason":"allowed"},{"i":2,"status":201,"queued":true,"reason":"allowed"},{"i":3,"status":201,"queued":true,"reason":"allowed"},{"i":4,"status":201,"queued":true,"reason":"allowed"},{"i":5,"status":201,"queued":true,"reason":"allowed"}]
CONTROL queue x5 with cap 2 -> [{"i":1,201,queued},{"i":2,201,queued},{"i":3,"status":409,"queued":false,"reason":"frequency_cap"},{"i":4,409,frequency_cap},{"i":5,409,frequency_cap}]
d1_before:
crm_automation_policy: [{"policy_key":"marketing:whatsapp","enabled":1,"quiet_start_hour":null,"quiet_end_hour":null,"max_contacts":0,"window_hours":24,"max_attempts":3,"retry_minutes":5,"updated_by":"ops.admin@pawspace.test"}]
crm_automation_dispatches: 0 rows
customer_contact_preferences: CUST-M with marketing_consent=1, service_consent=1, whatsapp_consent=1
d1_after:
cap=0: crm_automation_dispatches = 5 rows, all status='queued' for CUST-M / purpose='marketing'.
cap=2 (control): crm_automation_dispatches = 2 rows.
A cap of ZERO therefore admits strictly MORE traffic than a cap of two.
repeatable: yes - cap0 run executed twice in fresh worlds (cap0-RUN1, cap0-RUN2), 5/5 queued both times; the cap2 control blocked 3/5 in the same process
canonical_failure: lib/crm-automation-governance.ts, automationDecision: `if(policy.max_contacts&&policy.window_hours){...frequency cap...}` - the whole cap block is guarded on the TRUTHINESS of max_contacts, so the stored value 0 (and equally window_hours 0) is indistinguishable from NULL/'not configured' and the block never runs. The write side accepts 0 deliberately: app/api/crm-automation/route.ts POST save_policy validates only `if(value!==null&&value!==undefined&&(!Number.isFinite(value)||Number(value)<0))return json({error:"Automation limits must be non-negative numbers"},400)`. The neighbouring quiet-hours block in the same function shows the correct form - it tests `policy.quiet_start_hour!==null&&policy.quiet_start_hour!==undefined`, so quiet_start_hour=0 (midnight) works.
money_consequence: Unbounded per-message WhatsApp/SMS spend against a customer an operator was trying to protect: the operator sets the tightest cap the UI offers and gets no cap at all. Also the reputational cost of repeated marketing contact to one customer inside the configured window.
blast_radius: Every customer targeted under any crm_automation_policy row whose max_contacts or window_hours is 0. One mis-set policy key (e.g. marketing:whatsapp) removes the cap for the entire audience of that channel/purpose pair, not one customer.
regression: tests/ptja-w2b-consent-regressions.test.mjs :: "W2B-C03: a configured frequency cap of 0 allows nothing" + "W2B-C03: an unset cap still means unlimited, and a real cap still counts"
fix_note: The frequency-cap block was guarded on the TRUTHINESS of max_contacts, so a stored 0 was indistinguishable from NULL/not-configured and the cap never ran. It now tests for null explicitly, so a configured 0 means zero contacts allowed while an unset cap keeps meaning unlimited. The write side already accepts 0 deliberately.

title: Customer OTP login resolves a phone number with no precedence between primary and secondary, so the number's real owner is signed into a different customer's account
actor: CUSTOMER, unauthenticated, holding phone 9845012345 - which is CUST-OWNER's primary_phone and also happens to sit in CUST-NEIGHBOUR's secondary_phone column
request:
Through app/api/customer-otp/route.ts POST (env PAWSPACE_UAT_LOGIN=on, PAWSPACE_UAT_SIGNING_KEY 64 chars, PAWSPACE_IDENTITY_ASSERTION_SECRET_UAT 64 chars):
1) {"action":"request","phone":"9845012345"} -> sandbox challenge + sandboxCode
2) {"action":"verify","challengeId":"OTP-5D974E8A-BEA","code":"<sandboxCode>"}
Then, with the set-cookie session that returns:
3) GET /api/customer-profile
4) GET /api/customer-account
d1_after:
identity_bindings: [{"identity_source":"customer_otp","principal_key":"9845012345","subject_type":"customer","subject_id":"CUST-NEIGHBOUR","verification_state":"verified"}]
platform_identity_sessions: [{"subject_type":"customer","subject_id":"CUST-NEIGHBOUR","principal_key":"9845012345","role_code":"customer"}]
CUST-OWNER is untouched and now unreachable: the only phone that identifies them resolves to CUST-NEIGHBOUR, and the verified binding is durable, so every future login lands in the same wrong account.
repeatable: yes - run twice in fresh worlds (RUN1, RUN2), both returned customerId CUST-NEIGHBOUR and wrote the identical binding
canonical_failure: lib/customer-otp.ts:54 `let customer=await db.prepare("SELECT id,name,primary_phone,city_id FROM canonical_customers WHERE primary_phone=? OR secondary_phone=?").bind(phone,phone).first<Row>();` - one OR-ed predicate with no ORDER BY and no tie-break, so a secondary_phone match and a primary_phone match are equally authoritative and .first() takes whichever row the scan reaches first. There is also no uniqueness constraint on either phone column (schema in lib/customer-account.ts ensureCustomerAccountTables), so two rows carrying the same number is a representable state the query has no rule for.
money_consequence: No direct debit, but the resulting session can spend: the customer-account, booking, offers and reward surfaces all key off the session's customerId, so PawPoints, birthday rewards and review-reward coupons belonging to CUST-NEIGHBOUR are redeemable by whoever holds the phone. The larger cost is the disclosure itself - full name, both phone numbers, email, street address with flat number and pincode, and pet records.
blast_radius: Every canonical_customers pair where one row's secondary_phone equals another row's primary_phone - a state produced routinely by CSV imports and by households sharing a number. Reachable only where PAWSPACE_UAT_LOGIN=on and PAWSPACE_UAT_SIGNING_KEY is set (lib/uat-staging-auth.ts uatLoginEnabled); with the flag off the route returns 503 and the customer app cannot log in at all. Where the flag IS on over real customer data, every affected pair is a standing account takeover.
regression: tests/ptja-w2b-identity-takeover.test.mjs :: "W2B-C05: a planted secondary phone does not capture its real owner's login" + "W2B-C04: a primary-phone owner is not signed into a neighbour who lists it as secondary" + "W2B-C05: a profile write cannot claim a phone another customer already holds" + "W2B-C05: an ordinary profile update still works"
fix_note: Closed in both halves, which were both required. (1) lib/customer-otp.ts now resolves a login identity from primary_phone ONLY, through a newly exported resolveOtpCustomer so the rule is directly testable: a self-asserted phone is contact data, not a login identity. (2) lib/customer-account.ts update_profile refuses to claim a number that already belongs to another customer. Uniqueness alone would not have stopped a number nobody has registered yet from being planted, and precedence alone would not have stopped the claim. BEHAVIOUR CHANGE, stated plainly: someone whose number is recorded ONLY as a secondary is now signed in as a NEW customer rather than into the existing record. That is the safe direction and is what the platform already does for any number it has never seen.

title: A customer can claim any unverified phone number as their secondary, and the next person who OTP-signs-in with that number is dropped into the claimer's account
actor: Step 1: CUSTOMER platform session for CUST-ATTACKER (customer_otp binding, role_code=customer). Step 2: a different, unauthenticated person who genuinely holds phone 9845012345 and has never signed up.
response:
1) 201 {"data":{"customerId":"CUST-ATTACKER","action":"update_profile","entityId":"CUST-ATTACKER","duplicatePrevented":false}}
3) 200 {"data":{"customerId":"CUST-ATTACKER","customerName":"Mallory","phone":"9845012345","expiresAt":1787718277707}}   <-- the victim is signed in as Mallory
d1_before:
canonical_customers: [{"id":"CUST-ATTACKER","name":"Mallory","primary_phone":"9700000001","secondary_phone":null}]  - the victim has no row at all
platform_identity_sessions: one row, CUST-ATTACKER's own session
d1_after:
canonical_customers: [{"id":"CUST-ATTACKER","name":"Mallory","primary_phone":"9700000001","secondary_phone":"9845012345"}]  - NO new customer row was created for the victim
platform_identity_sessions: [{"subject_type":"customer","subject_id":"CUST-ATTACKER","principal_key":"customer:CUST-ATTACKER"},{"subject_type":"customer","subject_id":"CUST-ATTACKER","principal_key":"9845012345"}]  - the victim's verified OTP session points at the attacker's customer id. Everything the victim now enters (address, pets, bookings, PawPoints) is written under CUST-ATTACKER and is readable from the attacker's own session.
repeatable: yes - the two-step chain ran twice in fresh worlds (RUN1, RUN2) with identical results both times

(a) lib/customer-account.ts mutateCustomerAccount, action=="update_profile": `secondaryPhone=p.secondaryPhone===null?null:(safe(p.secondaryPhone)||customer.secondary_phone||null)` then `UPDATE canonical_customers SET city_id=?,name=?,primary_phone=?,secondary_phone=?,email=?,...` - an arbitrary caller-supplied phone number is written with no OTP proof of possession and no uniqueness check against any other customer's numbers. Targets are people who have not yet created a canonical_customers row - i.e. every new customer - plus, per W2-B3-C04, existing customers whose row loses the scan-order tie. Same environment gate as C04: reachable where PAWSPACE_UAT_LOGIN=on; step 1 alone (planting an unverified number on your own record) works regardless of that flag.

(1) lib/customer-otp.ts now resolves a login identity from primary_phone ONLY, through a newly exported resolveOtpCustomer so the rule is directly testable: a self-asserted phone is contact data, not a login identity. (2) lib/customer-account.ts update_profile refuses to claim a number that already belongs to another customer. Uniqueness alone would not have stopped a number nobody has registered yet from being planted, and precedence alone would not have stopped the claim. BEHAVIOUR CHANGE, stated plainly: someone whose number is recorded ONLY as a secondary is now signed in as a NEW customer rather than into the existing record. That is the safe direction and is what the platform already does for any number it has never seen.

title: A caller-supplied asOf on the staff-alert sweep fabricates SLA breaches and enqueues premature 'your case is overdue' messages to real customers, permanently suppressing the genuine notice
actor: STAFF role=admin (ops.admin@pawspace.test); the sweep branch requires customers.manage, held by admin and manager. The same code path is reachable via POST /api/staff-alert-runner (settings.manage).
response:
1) 201, case CASE-0060F894-766 created with first_response_due_at = now+90min, manager_escalation_due_at = now+180min, resolution_due_at = now+1080min - none of them overdue.
2) 200 {"data":{"created":3,"customerNotifications":{"attempted":2,"enqueued":2,"suppressed":0,"duplicatePrevented":0,"skipped":0,"errors":[],"transport":"canonical_chat_outbox","externalDelivery":false,"unavailable":false}}}
CONTROL (asOf=now): 200 created=0, customerNotifications {"attempted":0,"enqueued":0,...} and zero rows written anywhere - so the effect is entirely the asOf value.
FOLLOW-UP: sweep#1 asOf=FUTURE -> enqueued 2; sweep#2 at the REAL breach time -> {"attempted":2,"enqueued":0,"duplicatePrevented":2}; communication_messages total stays 2.
d1_before:
unified_cases: one open customer_complaint for CUST-1 with all three SLA timestamps in the future.
staff_alerts: 0 rows. communication_messages: 0 rows. communication_outbox: 0 rows.
canonical_customers: CUST-1 / 'Meera' / 9845012345, city blr. No communication_preferences row (consent unknown).
repeatable: yes - FUTURE-RUN1 and FUTURE-RUN2 in fresh worlds both produced created=3 and enqueued=2; the asOf=now control produced 0/0 in the same process
canonical_failure: app/api/staff-alerts/route.ts POST: `if(body.asOf!=null&&!Number.isFinite(Number(body.asOf)))return json({error:"asOf must be a finite epoch-milliseconds number"},400)` - the only check on asOf is finiteness; there is no upper bound at the present moment. The value flows into lib/staff-alert-center.ts runStaffAlertSweep as `const asOf=input.asOf??Date.now()` and from there into every `due_at<=?` predicate, notably caseAlerts (`WHERE status NOT IN ('resolved','closed') AND (first_response_due_at<=? OR manager_escalation_due_at<=? OR resolution_due_at<=?)`) and caseCustomerNotifications (same predicate), which then calls enqueueCommunication with `idempotencyKey:`case:${caseId}:customer:${item.kind}``. Because that key does not include the sweep time, the premature message permanently occupies the slot: the real escalation later returns duplicatePrevented and the customer is never told when the SLA actually breaches. app/api/staff-alert-runner/route.ts carries the identical unbounded check.
money_consequence: Per-message outbound spend on notices that were not due, at whatever multiple the case backlog is (one sweep touches every open case with a future due date at once, not one case). Worse commercially: the genuine breach notice is then never sent, so the service-recovery contact the SLA machinery exists to guarantee silently does not happen - and the alerts it created also mark healthy cases as 'critical - resolution overdue', pulling manager time onto cases that are inside SLA.
blast_radius: Every open unified_case with any SLA timestamp set - i.e. the entire live case backlog in one call - and every customer attached to one with a booking_id. Both /api/staff-alerts (customers.manage) and /api/staff-alert-runner (settings.manage) accept the parameter. The staff_alerts side is recoverable; the communication idempotency keys are not.
status: FIXED — narrowed to the irreversible half after measurement
regression: tests/ptja-w2b-consent-regressions.test.mjs :: "W2B-C06: a future sweep clock sends no customer notices" + "W2B-C06: a genuinely overdue case at the real clock still notifies"
fix_note: Customer notices are skipped when the sweep clock is in the future. The finding proposed bounding asOf at the ROUTE; I tried that first and it broke three existing tests in tests/alerting-hardening.test.mjs, which drive the runner route with asOf NOW+1min and NOW+3min to prove an alert fires once and auto-resolves as the clock clears. So a future asOf is a capability the platform deliberately has and tests, and the finding's own words name the right boundary: 'The staff_alerts side is recoverable; the communication idempotency keys are not.' A staff alert raised early can be resolved; a customer notice cannot be unsent, and because its idempotency key omits the sweep clock the GENUINE later notice is then permanently duplicatePrevented. The bound is therefore on the notification half only.

title: REFUTED: the ?customerId= parameter on the customer self-service family is NOT a cross-tenant read - provider, foreign-customer and anonymous callers are all refused, including where the gateway is deliberately open
domain: customer self-service surfaces (support-case, account, offers, vaccination, emergency, booking-rating, service-review, pet-birthday)
actor: Three attackers, each against the same seeded victim CUST-VICTIM: (a) a real partner_otp platform session for PRV-ATTACKER (role service_provider), (b) a real customer_otp platform session for CUST-OTHER, (c) no credentials at all
request:
GET with an explicit ?customerId=CUST-VICTIM against every route in the family that takes one, driven through the real route module AND through lib/api-gateway.ts authorizeApiRequest:
/api/customer-support-case, /api/customer-account, /api/customer-offers, /api/pet-vaccination, /api/pet-emergency, /api/booking-rating, /api/service-review, /api/pet-birthday
d1_before: canonical_customers CUST-VICTIM ('Meera Victim', 9845012345, meera@example.com); customer_addresses ADDR-V '12 Victim Lane, Indiranagar, Bengaluru 560038'; unified_cases CASE-V customer_complaint 'Groomer hurt my dog' / 'Bleeding paw after grooming' for CUST-VICTIM. identity_bindings + platform_identity_sessions carry a verified provider session for PRV-ATTACKER and a verified customer session for CUST-OTHER.
d1_after: Unchanged. No victim row appeared in any response body - the refusals carry only the error string.
repeatable: yes - each of the three attacker classes was driven against the whole route list in one pass and every call refused; the pattern is uniform, not sampled
canonical_failure: n/a - refutation. The guard that holds is lib/server-auth.ts requireCustomerOwnership (lines 81-88): the `hasPermission(actor.permissions,"customers.manage")||hasPermission(actor.permissions,"bookings.manage")` staff bypass is NOT satisfied by the service_provider role, whose permissions are exactly ["bookings.view","scheduling.view","communications.call","communications.message","self_service.view"] (lib/platform-security.ts:25), so the provider falls through to the identity-binding check and is refused on subject mismatch. Note the routes that matter here are gateway permission=null by design (lib/api-gateway.ts:14-15 lists /api/customer-support-case, /api/customer-account, /api/booking-rating), so the handler is the ONLY gate - and it holds.

title: REFUTED: the caller-supplied recipient on POST /api/communications action=dispatch_external_uat cannot be pointed at another customer - the boundary refuses before any outbound call
actor: STAFF role=admin (ops.admin@pawspace.test), holding communications.manage. Env configured as a fully live UAT dispatch path: PAWSPACE_COMMUNICATION_ENV=uat, provider URL set, provider token set, PAWSPACE_COMMUNICATION_UAT_ALLOWLIST="9700000009,9845012345", adapter whatsapp/limechat set to sandbox_ready + credentials configured.
request:
1) POST /api/communications {"action":"enqueue","customerId":"CUST-A","cityId":"blr","channel":"whatsapp","purpose":"transactional","bookingId":"BKG-A","idempotencyKey":"idem-RUN1","templateKey":"t"}
Then three dispatch attempts on that same messageId:
2) {"action":"dispatch_external_uat","messageId":"MSG-F748C356-0F47-","adapterName":"limechat","recipient":"9845012345"}  - CUST-B's phone, deliberately ON the allowlist
3) same with "recipient":"9111111111" - belongs to nobody
4) same with "recipient":"9800000001" - CUST-A's own phone but not allowlisted
globalThis.fetch was replaced with a stub that throws and counts, so no real outbound call was possible from this probe (this is the only boundary stubbed).
d1_before: canonical_customers: CUST-A 'Alice' 9800000001, CUST-B 'Bob' 9845012345. communication_messages/outbox empty before the enqueue.
d1_after:
communication_outbox: [{"message_id":"MSG-F748C356-0F47-","status":"queued","attempt_count":0}] - still queued, attempt_count NOT incremented, so a refused dispatch does not burn a retry either.
communication_messages: [{"id":"MSG-F748C356-0F47-","customer_id":"CUST-A","status":"queued","provider":null,"provider_reference":null}] - no provider recorded.
repeatable: yes - RUN1 and RUN2 in fresh worlds, all three refusals identical and fetchAttempts=0 both times
canonical_failure: n/a - refutation. Two independent guards hold, in lib/communication-provider-boundary.ts dispatchExternalCommunication: `if(!allowlisted(env,input.recipient))return{status:"recipient_not_allowlisted",...}` and then `if(!await recipientBelongsToCustomer(db,text(message.customer_id),text(message.channel),input.recipient))return{status:"recipient_customer_mismatch",...}`, the second comparing the recipient against the MESSAGE's customer_id's own primary_phone/secondary_phone (or email for the email channel) after stripping non-digits. Being on the allowlist is not sufficient; the recipient must belong to the message's customer. A consent gate (dispatchConsent) sits behind both.
money_consequence: None - no misdirected message possible through this path.

title: GET /api/conversations returns every customer's unmasked primary phone, and the thread view returns payload customerPhone and internalNote, to the associate role which lacks customers.view_full_phone
actor: STAFF role=associate (assoc@pawspace.test). Permissions measured at runtime: communications.manage = true, customers.view_full_phone = false.
request:
1) gateway: authorizeApiRequest(GET https://uat.pawspace.in/api/conversations, headers oai-authenticated-user-email: assoc@pawspace.test ...)
2) GET https://uat.pawspace.in/api/conversations   (app/api/conversations/route.ts GET, thread list)
3) GET https://uat.pawspace.in/api/conversations?threadId=THREAD-V   (same route, single thread)
d1_before:
canonical_customers: CUST-V 'Meera Victim' primary_phone '+919845012345' secondary_phone '+919845099999'.
communication_threads: THREAD-V for CUST-V, booking BKG-V, status open.
communication_messages: MSG-V on THREAD-V with payload_json {"customerPhone":"+919845012345","internalNote":"Customer threatened to go to consumer court; do not escalate to founder"}.
app_users: USR-ASSOC assoc@pawspace.test role_code='associate' status='active'.
d1_after: Unchanged - both calls are reads. The exposure is entirely in the response bodies quoted above.
repeatable: yes - RUN1 and RUN2 in fresh worlds returned byte-identical bodies
canonical_failure: Two expressions, one route. (a) lib/conversation-governance.ts listConversationThreads: `let query="SELECT t.*,c.name customer_name,c.primary_phone FROM communication_threads t LEFT JOIN canonical_customers c ON c.id=t.customer_id"` and then `threads.push({...row,customer_name:String(row.customer_name||"Customer"),primary_phone:row.primary_phone?String(row.primary_phone):null,...})` - the phone is deliberately joined in and emitted raw, with no reference to the caller's permissions. (b) app/api/conversations/route.ts GET: `const data=await getConversation(db,threadId,"staff")` - the scope is hardcoded to "staff", and getConversation only strips `payload.internalNote`, `payload.providerPhone` and `payload.customerPhone` when `scope!=="staff"`, so an associate holding communications.manage receives the internal-note and customer-phone fields the redaction branch exists to remove. The permission that admits the caller (communications.manage) is held by admin, manager AND associate (lib/platform-security.ts defaultRoles), while customers.view_full_phone is held by admin alone; the platform's own convention for this decision is app/api/subscription-customers/route.ts:42 `const reveal=hasPermission(actor.permissions,"customers.view_full_phone");`.
money_consequence: No money moves. The exposed assets are the customer contact list (one raw mobile per conversation thread, unbounded across the 100-thread pages) and free-text internal handling notes about the customer - here a note recording a threatened consumer-court complaint - visible to the lowest customer-facing staff tier and to anyone who obtains an associate account.
blast_radius: Every communication_threads row with a matching canonical_customers row - i.e. every customer who has ever been messaged - at up to 200 per call, plus every message payload on any thread whose id the caller can name. Affects the associate role today; the same hardcoded "staff" scope would admit any future role granted communications.manage.
status: FIXED (phone/name); internalNote visibility OPEN pending a product decision
regression: tests/ptja-w2b-exposure-regressions.test.mjs :: "W2B-C07: the conversation thread list masks the customer phone"
fix_note: Masked at the route, applying the convention app/api/subscription-customers/route.ts already carries: reveal = hasPermission(actor.permissions,'customers.view_full_phone'), then maskPhone/maskName. PARTIAL BY DESIGN: email is NOT masked - the platform defines only maskPhone and maskName - and whether an associate should see a customer's email at all is a product decision left open, the same call as for Customer 360. Applied to BOTH branches - the thread list and the single-thread view, whose message payload also carried customerPhone. The payload's internalNote (measured content: 'Customer threatened to go to consumer court; do not escalate to founder') is deliberately left alone: who may read a staff-authored internal note is a product decision, not a masking rule.

title: Two separate consent stores: a marketing opt-out recorded through /api/communications is honoured by the governed outbox and completely ignored by CRM automation, which queues the campaign anyway
actor: STAFF role=admin (ops.admin@pawspace.test). Customer CUST-X, whose marketing opt-out is the subject.
d1_before:
canonical_customers: CUST-X 'Meera' 9845012345, city blr.
After step 2 the two consent tables disagree, and both are the platform's own:
  communication_preferences: [{"customer_id":"CUST-X","service_updates":1,"marketing":0,"preferred_channel":null,"timezone":"Asia/Kolkata","source":"customer_opt_out_request"}]
  customer_contact_preferences: [{"customer_id":"CUST-X","marketing_consent":1,"service_consent":1,"whatsapp_consent":1,"opt_out":0,"source":"staff_review"}]
d1_after:
communication_messages: [{"customer_id":"CUST-X","purpose":"marketing","status":"suppressed"}]  - engine A blocked it
crm_automation_dispatches: [{"id":"AUTO-675695D3-8B7","customer_id":"CUST-X","journey_code":"winback","channel":"whatsapp","purpose":"marketing","status":"queued"}]  - engine B queued it, to the same customer, on the same channel, for the same purpose, minutes after the opt-out was recorded
repeatable: yes - RUN1 and RUN2 in fresh worlds, identical suppressed-vs-queued split both times
canonical_failure: The two outbound engines read different tables and neither reads the other's. lib/communication-engine.ts `consent()` reads `SELECT * FROM communication_preferences WHERE customer_id=?` and falls back to canonical_customers.consent_json; lib/crm-automation-governance.ts `automationDecision` reads `SELECT marketing_consent,service_consent,whatsapp_consent,sms_consent,email_consent FROM customer_contact_preferences WHERE customer_id=?` and decides on `if(input.purpose==="marketing"&&!Boolean(Number(consent?.marketing_consent||0)))`. communication_preferences is never consulted there. The write sides are equally split: app/api/communications/route.ts action=="preference" writes only communication_preferences (via setCommunicationPreference), app/api/customer-360/route.ts action=="update_consent" writes only customer_contact_preferences. lib/haptik-outbound-governance.ts and lib/whatsapp-uat-adapter.ts also read only customer_contact_preferences, so the same blind spot covers those senders.
money_consequence: Marketing messages billed and delivered to a customer who is on record as having opted out - the exact contact the opt-out was recorded to prevent - with a per-message channel cost and a compliance exposure the platform's own audit trail documents against it (securityAudit records the opt-out as 'communication.preference').
blast_radius: Every customer whose consent decision was captured on one surface and whose outbound goes through the other. Both directions are live: /api/crm-automation, lib/haptik-outbound-governance.ts and lib/whatsapp-uat-adapter.ts see only customer_contact_preferences; /api/communications, the customer-reminder sweep, the lifecycle-reminder engine and the staff-alert case notifications all see only communication_preferences. Any campaign run through the CRM automation engine ignores every opt-out ever recorded on the communications preference API.
regression: tests/ptja-w2b-consent-regressions.test.mjs :: "W2B-C08: an opt-out recorded on the communications API blocks CRM automation too" + "W2B-C08: a customer who has opted in on both stores is still reachable"
fix_note: automationDecision now also consults communication_preferences: an opt-out recorded in EITHER store blocks. Neither table was made the winner, because picking one would silently discard the other's decisions; silence in a store is not an opt-out, so an opted-in customer stays reachable. This fails closed. NOTE the two stores still exist and are still written by different surfaces - unifying them is a data-model decision that is carried forward, not taken here.

title: Deactivating a lifecycle reminder rule does nothing: the rule reads active=0 in the directory and the engine queues and delivers that exact reminder on the very next run
actor: STAFF role=founder (founder@pawspace.test) - /api/lifecycle-reminders requires settings.manage on both GET and POST
d1_before:
canonical_bookings: BKG-R, CUST-R, service_code='grooming', status='completed', scheduled_end 30 days ago; no future grooming booking.
lifecycle_reminder_rules: rule-grooming-rebook active=0 after step 1.
communication_messages: 0 rows. communication_outbox: 0 rows. reminder_governance_events: 0 rows.
d1_after:
communication_messages: [{"customer_id":"CUST-R","purpose":"lifecycle","template_key":"grooming_rebooking_reminder","status":"sandbox_delivered"}]
communication_outbox: [{"message_id":"MSG-0017A5F7-0AAE-","status":"sandbox_delivered"}]
reminder_governance_events: [{"customer_id":"CUST-R","reminder_type":"grooming_rebooking","cycle_key":"grooming_rebooking:CUST-R:2"}]
The message went through the real outbox and was consumed by the governed UAT sink (lib/customer-reminder-governance.ts consumeCustomerReminderSandboxOutbox); no external provider was contacted, because no external adapter is wired for the lifecycle purpose today. The outbox row is the send.
repeatable: yes - RUN1 and RUN2 in fresh worlds both showed active=0 in the directory and queued=1 from the same run_now
canonical_failure: lib/lifecycle-reminder-engine.ts runLifecycleReminderEngine: `const existingGoverned = await runCustomerReminderSweep(db, input); const directory = await lifecycleReminderDirectory(db); return { existingGoverned, policySummary: {...} }` - it calls the sweep and then reads the rule table, but never passes a rule, a filter or an active flag into it. lib/customer-reminder-governance.ts generateGroomingRebookingReminders and generateSubscriptionReminders never read lifecycle_reminder_rules at all; their only configuration input is `currentCadencePolicy(db)`, which reads reminder_cadence_policies. lifecycle_reminder_rules.active is written by saveLifecycleReminderRule and read only by lifecycleReminderDirectory, which reports it back to the screen - so `active` is a display field, not a control. The three seeded 'active: true' rules and the nine 'configuration_required' ones are equally inert in both directions.
money_consequence: Outbound reminder volume that operations believes it has stopped keeps being generated and billed once a live adapter is attached to the lifecycle purpose - the switch that exists to stop spend does not stop it. Symmetrically, the nine rules the directory reports as awaiting approval (new_customer welcome, existing_customer re-engagement, and rebooking for training/boarding/sitting/dog_walking/pet_taxi/food/relocation) would not start sending if activated, so an operator who turns one ON also gets nothing.
blast_radius: Every customer matched by the grooming-rebooking, subscription-unused-session and subscription-renewal sweeps - the whole eligible base each run - regardless of the state of the rule table. Both entry points are affected: POST /api/lifecycle-reminders run_now and POST /api/customer-reminders run_sweep_now call the same sweep, and the background scheduler runs it too.
status: FIXED — grooming exactly; subscription pair at rule-set granularity
regression: tests/ptja-w2b-consent-regressions.test.mjs :: "W2B-C09: a deactivated grooming rebooking rule stops the sweep generating it" + "W2B-C09: an active rule still generates"
fix_note: runCustomerReminderSweep now consults lifecycle_reminder_rules before running each generator. The gate sits in the sweep rather than the engine because three entry points reach it - /api/lifecycle-reminders run_now, /api/customer-reminders run_sweep_now and the background scheduler - and only the first goes through the engine. The mapping is the platform's own: rule-grooming-rebook names the grooming generator, rule-subscription-unused / rule-subscription-renewal name the subscription one. A missing rule row means the cadence was never governed, which is not the same as paused, so it still runs.
carried_forward: The subscription generator serves TWO rules and is skipped only when BOTH are inactive; deactivating one of that pair alone still runs it. Per-rule granularity there means teaching the generator which rule each reminder belongs to, which is a larger change than this correction and is recorded rather than half-done silently.

title: Unauthenticated POST /api/meet-and-greet has no rate limit and mints a fresh synthetic customer id per call, so the one-open-request-per-host cap never fires and a named host's queue can be flooded
actor: Anonymous, no credentials, one IP (cf-connecting-ip: 203.0.113.9). The gateway maps POST /api/meet-and-greet to permission=null by design.
request:
1) gateway: authorizeApiRequest(POST https://uat.pawspace.in/api/meet-and-greet, no credentials)
2) ten identical POSTs from the same IP:
   POST https://uat.pawspace.in/api/meet-and-greet, header cf-connecting-ip: 203.0.113.9, body {"format":"phone","hostProviderId":"PRV-HOST-1","preferredAt":<now+7d+i*60000>,"notes":"spam <i>"}
3) staff check: GET /api/meet-and-greet?hostProviderId=PRV-HOST-1 with admin headers
d1_before: meet_greet_requests: 0 rows. boarding_host_profiles: PRV-HOST-1 (a real, eligible boarding host). No credentials or session of any kind exists.
d1_after: meet_greet_requests: 10 rows, all host_provider_id='PRV-HOST-1', all status='requested', with 10 DISTINCT customer_id values: MGENQ-6F65340C-737, MGENQ-11B027CD-A10, MGENQ-6B847FE3-9B8, ... Each row also generated its meet_greet_events trail. Nothing links them, so no cap or dedupe can ever see them as one requester.
repeatable: yes - RUN1 and RUN2 in fresh worlds, 10/10 accepted and 10 distinct synthetic customer ids both times
canonical_failure: app/api/meet-and-greet/route.ts POST: the anonymous branch `} else { customerId = \`MGENQ-${crypto.randomUUID().slice(0, 12).toUpperCase()}\`; }` gives every anonymous call a brand-new identity, and lib/meet-and-greet.ts createMeetGreetRequest's only volume control is keyed to that identity: `SELECT id FROM meet_greet_requests WHERE customer_id=? AND host_provider_id=? AND status IN ('requested','confirmed') LIMIT 1` ... `if (open) throw new Error("An open meet & greet already exists with this host")`. A fresh id per request means `open` is always null. The route has no abuse gate of any kind - contrast app/api/public-contact/route.ts, the platform's other unauthenticated write, which runs `await enforceAbuseGate(db,request,now)` (5 per 10 minutes per hashed cf-connecting-ip) before it writes, and which W2-B3-R03 measured working.
money_consequence: No direct charge - meet_greet_requests are priced but not collected at this stage. The cost is operational: every row lands in the staff meet-and-greet directory as real work against a named host, and each is individually confirm/cancel/no_show-able only by a human with bookings.manage, so clearing a flood is manual. A host's queue can be buried, and genuine requests to that host become indistinguishable from noise.
blast_radius: Any provider id that passes hostEligible (present in boarding_host_profiles, or a provider_capacity_profiles row whose services_json mentions pet_sitting) - i.e. every live boarding host and pet-sitting provider, individually targetable by name. Unbounded volume from a single IP; the only limits observed were the format/time validations, which the attacker satisfies trivially.
regression: tests/ptja-w2b-crm-media-authz.test.mjs :: "W2B-C10: anonymous meet & greet requests from one origin are bounded" + "W2B-C10: a caller with no determinable origin is refused, and the first few still work"
fix_note: The anonymous branch is bounded per origin using the gate app/api/public-contact/route.ts already carried - the one this sweep's own R03 independently confirmed is exact at its limit and fails closed with no IP. It was extracted into lib/public-abuse-gate.ts rather than copied, so the two endpoints cannot drift, and meet-and-greet uses its own table so neither consumes the other's budget. COLLATERAL, stated: tests/meet-and-greet-request-identity.test.mjs built its requests with no cf-connecting-ip, which the gate refuses. Each case now sends its own caller IP - as Cloudflare always does in production, and distinct per case so the shared per-origin budget cannot couple them. What those tests assert, that an enquiry stays public and needs no session or access code, is unchanged.

title: REFUTED: the public contact-form abuse gate is not off-by-one or bypassable by a missing IP header - it admits exactly 5 per window and fails closed without an IP
request: Eight identical POSTs to /api/public-contact from cf-connecting-ip 203.0.113.9 with body {"name":"Spam Bot","phone":"9845012345","email":"a@b.co","area":"Indiranagar","petNames":"X","service":"Grooming","message":"hi"}, then one POST with NO cf-connecting-ip header, then one from a different IP (203.0.113.10).
response:
[{"i":1,201},{"i":2,201},{"i":3,201},{"i":4,201},{"i":5,201},{"i":6,"status":429,"body":"Too many contact requests. Please try again later."},{"i":7,429},{"i":8,429}]
no cf-connecting-ip -> 429 {"error":"Request origin could not be verified"}  (fails CLOSED, not open)
different IP -> 201 {"ok":true,"leadId":"LEAD-f6d5ca29-..."}  (per-IP, as intended)
d1_after:
crm_contacts: 5 rows from the flooding IP (the 429s wrote nothing), 6 after the second IP's single accepted lead.
public_contact_rate_limits: [{"attempts":8}] - the counter keeps incrementing on refused attempts, so a client cannot ride the limit down by retrying.
repeatable: yes - RUN1 and RUN2 in fresh worlds, identical 5-accepted/3-refused split and identical fail-closed behaviour
canonical_failure: n/a - refutation. app/api/public-contact/route.ts enforceAbuseGate increments first and then tests `if(!state||Number(state.attempts)>RATE_LIMIT)` with RATE_LIMIT=5: because the increment precedes the test, attempt 6 reads attempts=6 and is refused, so the >-rather-than->= comparison is correct here and not off by one. fingerprintFor throws governedJsonError 429 when cf-connecting-ip is absent, so a spoof-by-omission is refused rather than sharing one bucket.
